decisions.reason: Although this consumer-facing superfood drink mix sits less centrally in the firm's industrial-technology profile and was only lightly promoted, it still builds on the existing offer and a young, growth-oriented R&D firm would usually give such a recent launch more time before admitting failure.

These modular waste-to-energy plant extensions are tightly aligned with the firm's core business and long-term strategic direction, so prior engineering investment and the need to justify that commitment make withdrawal unlikely after only one year.

A waste-oil-to-energy plant appears to involve substantial development effort and it had its own webpage, indicating visible public commitment that under escalation-of-commitment logic strongly favors continuing with it.

The plastic-waste-to-fuel plant is close to the firm's established sustainability and conversion technologies, and despite somewhat less visible commitment than Product C the likely sunk R&D and prototyping costs support keeping it on the market.
